verified.todo_source:
# Keep track of what needs doing.
app Todos
Given
 Todo { title:text trim min=1 max=200 label="Task", done:bool=false label={text="Status",values={true="Done",false="Open"}} } label="Todo"
 policy Todo read=members
 fixture task=Todo {title="Try Can"}
When
 crud Todo by=members fields=title,done label={create="Add task"}
  examples update record=task
   as,changes.done,request.record.version -> record.done
   members,true,1 -> true
   members,true,0 -> error(conflict)
   public,true,1 -> error(forbidden)
Then
 preferences { view:enum(all,open,done)=all label={text="Show",values={all="All",open="Open",done="Done"}} }
 page / title="Todos"
  card "Add a task"
   form Todo.create fields=title display=inline
    input title
  card "Your tasks"
   tabs preferences.view
   list Todo as task where preferences.view==all or (preferences.view==open and not task.done) or (preferences.view==done and task.done) order=-created search=title empty="No tasks here. Add a task or choose another view."
    text row.title,row.done
    edit fields=title,done
    tooltip "Permanently delete this task"
     delete
verified.record_syntax: Existing Can records use comma-separated NAME=value members; nested records exist.
verified.current_styling: Then has finite producer-catalog component appearance and core card layout=stack|columns, but no generic per-component spacing/sizing/responsive styling. CSS acquisition currently uses prebuilt daisyUI plus manually supplied utilities. No proposed syntax is implemented.

state.context: A user wants a concise CSS abbreviation per Then component, with responsive variation and a complete Todo illustration. Treat records, direct options and utility strings equally as future syntax, all capable of the same bounded CSS output. Judge adoption, easy reading, token economy, diagnosable mistakes and mobile-first layout control. Verified current Can has nested comma-separated NAME=value records, preset appearance options and limited card layouts, without a generic style language. Its common left desktop sidebar/small-screen hamburger remains implicit. Styling must preserve the existing operations, defaults, grants, credentials, optimistic versions and archive deletion.
state.shared_semantics: Each alternative gets identical validation and targeting rules: literal typed style values with pinned numeric spacing and checked dimension strings; per-component root plus declared body/row parts; static emitted styles rather than arbitrary selectors. Component defaults precede base overrides, and active min-width scopes sm40rem, md48rem, lg64rem, xl80rem override by ascending threshold. A single scope may not assign the same expanded CSS property twice; later responsive scopes may replace it. Required inputs, errors and action semantics keep their standard behavior.

syntax.instructions: Given these shared semantics and the current language facts, which candidate is the best concise, maintainable way to write component CSS and responsive refinements?

criteria.map: Attach css={p=4,gap=3,sm={p=6}}. Structured nested records distinguish style names from operational options and enable completion, while adding a small punctuation wrapper and part subrecords.
criteria.attrs: Attach p=4 gap=3 sm={p=6} as ordinary-looking component options. This is shorter in simple cases but requires rules for collisions with existing option names; targeting uses direct part properties.
criteria.string: Attach css="p-4 gap-3 sm:p-6". Closed validated utility strings have concise familiar notation, with a separate token grammar for diagnostics, responsive values and generated-part prefixes.
criteria.defer: Decline to rank a syntax yet if all options leave important constraints unresolved; maintain proposal status.
